commitResults.messageBody:
Rename EVException to EvException, since an abbreviation used as part of
a longer name keeps only its first letter capitalised. Rename
TaskList.asList to getTasks, because method names must be verbs, and the
Ui field `in` to `scanner`, because a field's scope is too large for a
two-letter name.

Wrap the two lines in Storage that ran past the 110-character soft
limit, and initialise skippedLineCount where it is declared.

commitResults.messageTitle: Record the coding and commit standards in AGENTS.md
commitResults.messageBody:
The standard applies to all code added from now on, so the rules that
come up most in this project are written down where both the student and
any AI assistant working in this repository will read them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a find command to search task descriptions
commitResults.messageBody:
A long list is hard to scan, and the list and on commands can only show
everything or one date's worth. Add `find <keyword>`, which shows the
tasks whose description contains the keyword.

The search ignores capitalisation and matches part of a word, so `boo`
finds `book`. It looks at the description only: dates are no longer
stored as text, so matching them here would be inconsistent with how
they are shown. Matching tasks keep the number they have in the full
list, as the on command already does, so a task can be marked or deleted
without listing everything first.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test the find command
commitResults.messageBody:
Three UI test cases cover a plain search, case insensitive and partial
matches, and the two ways a search can come back with nothing to show.
Seven JUnit tests cover Task.hasKeyword and Parser.parseKeyword.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-Level-9 into master
Merge branch-A-JavaDoc into master
commitResults.messageBody:
Conflicts in Parser, Task and Ui: both branches added lines in the same
places, the find branch adding members and this branch adding the header
comments above them. Both sides are kept in each case.

The documentation branch was cut before find existed, so its members
arrived undocumented. Add header comments for Task.hasKeyword,
Parser.parseKeyword, Ui.showMatchingTasks and the FindCommand class, so
that every non-private class and method is documented as the increment
intended.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-CodingStandard into master
commitResults.messageBody:
Six files conflicted in the same way: this branch renamed the exception
class and reflowed a few lines, while master had added a header comment
directly above each signature. Keep the comments and apply the renames
to them as well, so that no @throws tag still names EVException.

EVException.java came in as a modify/delete conflict, because a rename
looks like a delete to Git and master had modified the old file. Resolve
it by keeping the rename and moving the header comments into
EvException.java.

Two changes needed redoing by hand after taking master's side of the
conflicts: TaskList.asList becomes getTasks, and the two Storage lines
that ran past the length limit stay wrapped. The find command and its
tests also still named EVException in places neither branch touched, so
Git reported no conflict there at all.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check the coding standard with Checkstyle
commitResults.messageBody:
The standard was being followed by hand and by review, which is how a
duplicate import survived in ParserTest: it was added on one branch and
merged without conflict, so nothing flagged it.

Add the Checkstyle plugin with the configuration from AddressBook
Level 3, which encodes the same SE-EDU standard this project already
follows. Checking is now part of `gradlew build`, so a violation fails
the build rather than waiting to be noticed.

Fix the 24 violations found: the duplicate import, and the arrow switch
cases in Parser and Storage, which the configuration wants indented one
level from the switch itself.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-CheckStyle into master
Add a JavaFX window for the chatbot
commitResults.messageBody:
Ui used to print each reply as it worded it, which a window cannot use.
It now only records what EV says, and a caller takes the text with
takeResponse. ConsoleUi overrides that to also print the reply between
divider lines, so the terminal keeps the exact output it had, dividers,
banner and scanner included, none of which belong in a window.

EV gains getResponse, which parses one line, runs the command and hands
back what Ui collected. The terminal loop and the window now differ only
in where the text goes; the commands, task list and storage are shared.

The JavaFX classes live in ev.gui so that the text UI test runner, which
compiles with plain javac and no JavaFX on its class path, can skip that
one folder. Launcher is separate from Main because a main class that
extends Application cannot be loaded before the toolkit is running.

All 36 text UI test cases still pass unchanged, which is the point: the
window is an addition, not a replacement.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-Level-10 into master
Build EvException messages from separate lines
commitResults.messageBody:
Nineteen of the twenty-six places that raise an EvException were joining
two lines by hand, one saying what went wrong and one showing what to
type instead. The line break is now the exception's business: its
constructor takes the lines as varargs and joins them.

The structure of these messages becomes visible in the code rather than
hidden inside a concatenation, a single-line message still needs no
special case, and the separator is stated once instead of nineteen
times.

Task.encode already used varargs for the fields a subclass adds to its
save line, which is the same idea applied to a different problem.

Output is unchanged: all 36 text UI cases compare the messages verbatim
and still pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-Varargs into master
Document internal assumptions with assertions
commitResults.messageBody:
Several assumptions hold everywhere in this code but are written down
nowhere: a line reaching the parser has already been checked for being
blank, a keyword reaching a task is never empty, and the window has been
given a chatbot before it accepts input. When one of them breaks, the
symptom shows up far from the cause, usually as a NullPointerException
or as silently wrong output.

State them as assertions, so a broken assumption reports itself at the
place it was broken. Two of them are postconditions rather than
preconditions: removing a task must shorten the list by exactly one, and
a save that did not throw must have left a file behind.

Assertions are for assumptions the code itself guarantees, so none of
these can be triggered by what the user types. A description containing
the field separator, for instance, is a real limitation but is left to
ordinary handling, because a user can cause it.

Turn assertions on where the code runs: -ea for the application and for
the text UI test runner. Gradle already enables them when running the
JUnit tests. Inverting one assertion was enough to make a UI test case
fail, which confirms they are live rather than dead code.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract the shared listing code in Ui
commitResults.messageBody:
Three methods showed a list of tasks and differed only in which tasks
they kept and how they worded the two outcomes. Everything else, walking
the list, numbering each entry by its position in the full list and
choosing between a heading and an empty-result sentence, was written out
three times.

Pass the filter and the two pieces of wording to one private method
instead. Each public method is now four lines that say what it selects
and what it calls the result, and a change to how a listing is formatted
happens in one place rather than three.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the two kinds of mark command at the call site
commitResults.messageBody:
The parser read `new MarkCommand(parseTaskNumber(argument), true)`,
where the boolean says nothing to a reader: which way the status is
going can only be learned by opening the constructor.

Make the constructor private and add mark and unmark factory methods, so
the call site names the operation. The class still keeps one boolean
field, since the two commands differ only in that flag and splitting
them into separate classes would duplicate the rest.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fail loudly when a view cannot be loaded
commitResults.messageBody:
Both places that load an FXML file printed the stack trace and carried
on. In DialogBox that guarantees a NullPointerException on the next
line, because the injected fields are still null, and the real cause,
a missing or misnamed view file, is by then buried above an unrelated
stack trace.

Throw instead, naming the file that could not be loaded. A missing view
is a packaging or path error rather than something the user did, so
there is nothing to recover from and stopping at the point of failure
is the most useful thing to do.

Also stop handing out the task list's backing list. getTasks returns an
unmodifiable view, so callers that only read it still see later changes,
while adding and removing stay with the class that owns the numbering.

commitResults.messageTitle: Express collection work as streams
commitResults.messageBody:
Four loops existed only to turn one collection into another value, and
each carried bookkeeping that had nothing to do with the intent.
listKeywords tracked whether a separator was still needed, save filled a
list one element at a time, the blank-field check looped in order to
answer a yes-or-no question, and the three listings in Ui each built a
string with an index of their own.

Say what is wanted instead: map to file lines, join keywords with a
separator, ask anyMatch whether a field is blank, and select the wanted
tasks with filter. The listings keep IntStream rather than streaming the
tasks directly, because the number shown is the position in the full
list, which is what lets a task found by a search be marked without
listing everything first.

The parsing loop in load keeps its for loop on purpose: it counts
unreadable lines as it goes and calls a method that throws a checked
exception, neither of which a stream expresses without becoming harder
to read than the loop it replaces.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge master into branch-A-Streams
commitResults.messageBody:
Both branches rewrote the three listing methods in Ui, for different
reasons: master to stop repeating the choice between a heading and an
empty-result sentence, this branch to build the numbered lines with a
stream instead of a StringBuilder and a hand-kept index.

Keep both. showSelected still decides what to say, and now asks
numberedListing for the lines, so the three public methods stay four
lines each and the counting stays in one stream.

Delete appendNumbered, which nothing calls once the stream produces the
lines. Git reports no conflict for code that simply stops being used, so
it has to be noticed by reading.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add an update command for editing a task
commitResults.messageBody:
Changing one detail of a task meant deleting it and typing it again from
scratch, which loses the done status and invites a typo in the parts
that were supposed to stay the same.

Add `update <number> <option> <value>`, where the option is /desc, /by,
/from or /to. Exactly one option is allowed per command: accepting
several would need a rule for what happens when the second one fails
after the first has already been applied, and typing two commands is no
harder than typing one.

Which options a task has is decided by the task, not by the command. A
todo takes /desc, a deadline adds /by, an event adds /from and /to, and
anything else is refused with the list of what that kind of task does
have. UpdateCommand therefore needs no instanceof, and a new kind of
task would not send anyone back to edit it.

An update that is refused changes nothing: the value is read before the
field is assigned. Times are read by the same parser the add commands
use, and an event may still end before it starts, as it may today when
it is first created.

The save format does not change, so existing files keep working.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #4 from Dai-yangjie/branch-C-Update

commitResults.messageTitle: Tell the two sides of the conversation apart
commitResults.messageBody:
Both speakers looked the same, a bubble with a picture beside it, which
is how two people chatting are drawn. This conversation is between a
person and an app, and their messages are not alike: what the user types
is short, while EV answers with numbered lists that a narrow bubble
squeezes into a column.

Give each side its own shape. The user keeps a compact bubble on the
right; EV's reply is flat text that takes the full width, in a
monospaced font so the status boxes of a list line up down the page.

Show a refusal differently from an answer. EV now reports whether the
last reply came from an exception, and the window styles those with a
red rule and a pale red ground, so an error is not read as a result.

Free up room while there: the avatars are a third of their old size and
clipped to circles, the input row sits flush with the window edge, and
the scroll bar has lost its end buttons.

The wording of every reply is untouched, so all 41 text UI cases still
pass; this commit only changes how the window presents them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-BetterGui into master
Give EV the voice of a suit assistant
commitResults.messageBody:
EV spoke like a form letter: "Got it. I've added this task:", "Nice!
I've marked this task as done:". Long, cheerful and interchangeable with
any other tutorial chatbot.

Rewrite every reply as the assistant in the suit would say it: short,
unbothered, no more words than the fact needs. Added. Done. Removed.
Your list:. Errors become a noun phrase and an example rather than a
sentence and an apology. EV greets Peter by name and signs off by name,
and nowhere else, because an assistant that says your name in every
breath sounds like a machine pretending.

The text stays ASCII. The console the text UI runs in is not always on a
UTF-8 code page, and 41 test cases compare its output character by
character.

The wording lives in one place, so this is a change to Ui, Parser,
CommandWord, TaskList, Task, Storage and DateTimes, plus the same
sentences where the test plan asserts them and the two the test runner
checks itself.

commitResults.messageTitle: Colour the window after the avatars
commitResults.messageBody:
EV now wears the mask and Peter the spider badge, so the window follows
them: Peter's messages sit in a dark bubble, EV answers behind a red
rule, and the send button is red because the window is EV's.

Errors move from red to amber. Red already means "EV is speaking", and a
warning in the same colour would be the one thing on screen saying two
things at once.

The avatars are cropped square and scaled to 128px, four times the size
they are shown at, so they stay sharp. EV's keeps 86 per cent of the
frame, which trims the cream border that would otherwise show as a ring
around the circular crop.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-Personality into master
Refuse the input that used to be quietly accepted
commitResults.messageBody:
Two of these were silent data faults rather than missing messages.

A day a month does not have was moved to the nearest real one, so
2019-02-30 became a task due on the 28th and nothing said so. Resolving
strictly refuses it, which is also why the patterns now spell the year
uuuu: strict mode will not resolve a year of era without an era.

A description holding a pipe was accepted, saved, and then dropped as
unreadable on the next start, because the pipe is what separates fields
in the save file. The task vanished overnight with no message at any
point. It is now refused while the user is still there to retype it.

The other three are input EV should never have taken. A second /by was
swallowed into the date, so the complaint named the date rather than the
repeated option. An event could end before it started, whether it was
being created or edited afterwards; the check now lives in the Event
constructor and in both update paths, so the object cannot reach that
state at all. Adding a task already on the list now says which task it
already is, and finishing a task does not make it a different one.

The test runner had its own version of the same problem: PowerShell
unrolls a one-element array leaving a statement block, so a save file of
exactly one line was compared character by character. No case had a
one-line file until now.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-MoreErrorHandling into master
Cover the classes the tests had been reaching only indirectly
commitResults.messageBody:
Comparing the production classes against the test classes left three
gaps. EV had no tests at all, although getResponse, isExit and
isErrorResponse are the whole of what the window talks to. The eight
command classes were exercised only end to end, so nothing asserted what
execute does to the list, the reply and the save file. Ui and ConsoleUi,
which own every sentence EV says, were checked only by running the app.

Add a test class for each, and for CommandWord and EvException. The
command tests assert all three effects together, since a command that
changes the list but forgets to save is the kind of fault that shows up
a day later. The EV tests cover a restart by writing with one instance
and reading with another, and they pin the error flag being cleared by
the next command that succeeds.

ConsoleUi is tested by capturing System.out, to confirm it both prints
between dividers and records the reply for takeResponse: that pairing is
what lets the terminal and the window share one chatbot.

The GUI classes are left to manual testing, as the increment allows.

Commenting out the line that clears Ui's buffer makes several of the new
tests fail, which is the check that they are testing something.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-MoreTesting into master
Write the user guide and finish naming the product
commitResults.messageBody:
The user guide was still the template's placeholder. Write it for
someone who has just downloaded the JAR: what the three kinds of task
are, how to write a date, then each command with a real example and the
reply it actually produces, and finally what EV does when a command
cannot be carried out.

Rename the save file from data/duke.txt to data/ev.txt. The path is not
only internal: it appears in the message about unreadable lines, so it
was one of the last places the old name still showed.

Turn the repository README from template instructions into a page about
the product, and give credit where it is due: the assistant that wrote
most of this code, the course materials the build and style
configuration come from, and the three images, each with the post it was
taken from and a note that they are fan art rather than freely licensed
work.

Add docs/Ui.png, a screenshot of the window in use, for the product
website.
